actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository is a multi-policy robot deployment framework based on a state-switching mechanism, with the included policies designed for the Unitree G1 robot (29-DoF)
The deployment framework applies only to G1 robots with a 3-DOF waist, and a waist fixing bracket must be unlocked before the framework can be used normally
The MuJoCo simulation is started with python deploy_mujoco/deploy_mujoco.py
The simulation configuration selects g1_description/scene.xml as the model, sets simulation_dt to 0.003 s and sets control_decimation to 7
The scene MJCF includes the robot model g1_29dof_rev_1_0.xml
The robot MJCF is model g1_29dof_rev_1_0, uses radian angles and keeps its meshes in meshes/
The robot MJCF sets its integration step to 0.002 s and selects the implicit integrator
The pelvis body starts at z 0.793 m and carries the free joint floating_base_joint
The left hip pitch joint has a range of -2.5307 to 2.8798 rad and an actuator force range of -88 to 88
The robot MJCF declares 29 motor actuators, one per joint from left_hip_pitch_joint to right_wrist_yaw_joint, and every motor element carries only name and joint attributes (no ctrlrange)
The robot MJCF defines four IMU sensors: a gyro and an accelerometer at imu_in_torso and imu_in_pelvis, each with a noise and cutoff value
The MuJoCo loop loads the scene with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path, creates MjData, overrides m.opt.timestep with simulation_dt and takes the actuator count from m.nu
The MuJoCo loop computes a PD torque from the policy output and writes it to d.ctrl before every mujoco.mj_step(m, d)

The MuJoCo loop runs control_decimation physics steps per policy update and reads qpos[7:], qvel[6:], qpos[3:7] and qvel[3:6] as joint positions, joint velocities, base quaternion and base angular velocity
The real robot configuration expects 29 joints and a control_dt of 0.02 s
The README reports that only the Charleston dance policy is verified stable on physical robots and that all other movements are not recommended for physical deployment

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the MJCF deterministically from the model defaults; the bridge accepts a seed in the reset input but does not use it, and a reset restores the model defaults, so one ctrl sequence repeats a trajectory on the same engine.  The package's fake is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the scene and the included robot MJCF for the 29 motor actuators, the joint dimensions and the 0.002 s model step, then moves each actuated joint by a placeholder velocity proportional to its control value; it computes no inertia, torque, contact, friction, equality or actuator dynamics, leaves the free base fixed and so produces no MuJoCo trajectory

the stand-in loads no STL mesh or texture and resolves no collision or contact; it does not apply the joint damping, armature or frictionloss defaults, the joint ranges or the actuator force ranges of the model

the upstream simulation overrides the model step with simulation_dt 0.003 from deploy_mujoco/config/mujoco.yaml:2 (deploy_mujoco/deploy_mujoco.py:30, :35), while this package serves the MJCF's own 0.002 s step; the control decimation 7, the PD gains and the policy layer are not part of this driver

the upstream simulation also runs the FSM, policy inference, joystick and viewer (deploy_mujoco/deploy_mujoco.py:43-106); this driver exposes only the MuJoCo ctrl vector and integration state, with no viewer, joystick or policy
the upstream real-robot deployment (deploy_real/deploy_real.py, unitree_sdk2) is not part of this simulated driver; no physical G1 is modelled or driven
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

operator_required.name: step
operator_required.reason: the model gives none of its actuators no control range (ctrllimited false or no ctrlrange), so MuJoCo leaves the control unclamped; site-limits.json must bound action.ctrl before a step can set it

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
